newsitem.title: USA: US Airways pilots say to meet with management.
newsitem.headline: US Airways pilots say to meet with management.

text.p: Pilots at US Airways Group Inc said they will meet with the airlines' management over the next ten days to discuss the development of a low-cost unit and continue labor contract talks.
Representatives from the Air Line Pilots Association said they will hold several meetings with management from April 1 to April 10. US Airways representatives could not be reached for comment.
The Arlington, Va.-based airline and its pilots have been mulling ways to create a new low-cost unit to compete with rivals such as Southwest Airlines Co.

Under a preliminary proposal, US Airways could convert up to 40 percent of its flying time or "block hours" into a new, low-cost service, sources said. The airline and its pilots are at odds about the size of the low-cost operations, the routes it would fly and the pay rates for those workers.
Contract negotiations with the pilots also continue, the pilots union said.

US Airways, which has one of the highest cost structures in the industry, has asked its pilots to accept pay cuts up to 12 percent. The proposed wage cuts come at a time when unions at rival carriers are seeking double-digit wage increases.
The low-cost service and the contract talks are part of US Airways' efforts to cut costs and remain competitive in the face of increased competition from regional and low-cost carriers.
US Airways' order for 400 Airbus Industrie aircraft depends on the airline achieving a "competitive cost structure."
